question: Heparin is the commonly used anticoagulant in cardiac surgery. All of the following are true about heparin except-

options.opa: Weakest acid found in living things
options.opb: Most commercial preparations of heparin now utilize pig intestinal slimes

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Heparin is an anticoagulant" -> "Inhibits thrombin and factor Xa" -> "Acts via Antithrombin activation" -> "True statement" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Heparin is derived from animal sources" -> "Most commercial preparations utilize pig intestinal mucosa" -> "True statement" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Heparin can cause a decrease in platelet count" -> "This condition is known as thrombocytopenia" -> "True statement" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Heparin is a polysaccharide" -> "It is not classified as an acid" -> "Weakest acid found in living things is incorrect" -> 85%
analysis: Heparin is a widely used anticoagulant that functions primarily through the activation of Antithrombin, which inhibits thrombin and factor Xa. This aligns with option (opc). Most commercial preparations of heparin are derived from pig intestinal mucosa, confirming option (opb) as true. Heparin can cause thrombocytopenia, a known side effect, making option (opd) accurate as well. However, heparin is a polysaccharide and does not fit the definition of an acid, let alone the 'weakest acid found in living things,' which makes option (opa) incorrect. Therefore, the statement about heparin being the weakest acid is the only false statement among the options provided.
